transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, yeah. Um, thanks. I came in because I just... I can’t shut my brain off anymore. It’s like it starts with one little concern, you know? Like the other day, a client wasn't responding to an email about a system migration. Which, honestly, those migrations are a total nightmare right now because corporate forced us to switch to this new cloud infrastructure, and half my IT team doesn't even have the right certifications for it yet. I told the director we needed more training budget, but they never listen, they just expect it to magically work on day one. My buddy Dave—he used to work over at Cisco—he was telling me they had the exact same issue last year and it took down their entire... wait, sorry, what was I saying? 

Right, the client. So the client isn't responding, and within minutes, my brain just spirals and I’m completely convinced I’ll lose the contract. And if I lose that, I’m going to fall behind on my divorce payments, and I'll just never get back to a real leadership role. It just goes zero to a hundred. Speaking of the divorce, she actually kept the house, which has this massive oak tree in the front yard that drops leaves into the gutters constantly. I used to spend every single Sunday up on a ladder cleaning those things out. I really don't miss those gutters, but... yeah, I just can't get my head to stop worrying.
Do you find that you worry about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

Yeah, constantly. It's exactly like that. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to the next—like, I'll be stressing about my contract work, and then suddenly I'm obsessing over the mortgage payments. Which, honestly, the housing market is completely insane right now. I was reading this article about how property taxes are going up again, and it’s just pricing normal people out. My neighbor—well, my old neighbor, before the divorce—he had to sell his boat just to cover his new escrow. Beautiful boat, too, a Sea Ray. We took it out on the Chesapeake a couple times, caught some decent rockfish... 

But anyway, yeah, the worry. It just jumps around. Like, out of nowhere I’ll start worrying about whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods. And there's usually no real reason for it, but if I get a delayed email from a recruiter, even by just a few hours, it suddenly feels like absolute proof that my whole career is closing down. Which is stupid because recruiters are terrible at replying anyway. I had this one headhunter last year who used to text me at, like, 9 PM on a Friday. Who texts about a senior developer role on a Friday night? I was trying to watch a movie... but, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, worrying about different things without a clear reason. Yeah. It's just... everything. All at once.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping, when you’re feeling this way?

Yeah, absolutely. I'm just wound up pretty much all day long. My shoulders feel like they're completely locked in place, like I'm just bracing myself for bad news 24/7. It's actually gotten so bad that my massage therapist—well, she's not really a massage therapist, she does this weird structural integration thing called Rolfing. Have you heard of it? It's intense. Like, she digs her elbows into your fascia and it hurts like hell, but it's supposed to realign your posture. My buddy Dave recommended her. He swore by it after he herniated a disc deadlifting, which, honestly, at our age, why are you still doing heavy deadlifts? He was trying to keep up with these 20-somethings at his CrossFit gym. CrossFit is basically a cult anyway, if you ask me. I tried it once and couldn't walk for three days. 

But anyway, what were we... right, physical stuff. Yeah, the tension is awful. And I just can't sit still. I end up pacing around the house, or if I'm stuck on a Zoom call, I'm just aggressively bouncing my leg under the desk. Even when there's literally nothing going on, no crisis, no fires to put out, I'm just vibrating with it. It's exhausting.
Have you felt this way — worrying a lot and feeling physically tense — more days than not over the past several months?

Yeah, more days than not, for sure. Honestly, it's been pretty much every day since I got fired. That was about thirteen months ago, and it just never really let up, even after I finally landed some contract work. Getting fired was a total blindside, by the way. I was at that company for eight years. Eight years! I built their entire backend infrastructure from scratch. And then they bring in this new VP of Engineering—guy was like 32, wore those weird minimalist toe shoes to the office. Who wears toe shoes to a corporate office? Anyway, he decided they needed to "streamline" and "synergize," which is just corporate speak for firing the expensive senior guys. 

I actually ran into him a couple of months ago at a Whole Foods. He was buying organic kale or something, and he had the nerve to act like we were old buddies. "Hey man, how's the contracting life treating you?" I almost threw my cold brew at him. Cold brew is a rip-off anyway, right? It's just iced coffee that they charge you double for because they let it sit in a bucket overnight. I started making my own at home with this French press my ex-wife left behind, but it never tastes the same. 

But, uh, wait, what was the question? Oh, how long it's been going on. Yeah, about thirteen months. Ever since they let me go. It's just been a constant hum of anxiety since then.

Do you find yourself getting intensely anxious about things that most people might consider minor or hypothetical, like a delayed email or a small work issue, even when there’s no clear evidence that anything is actually wrong?

Yeah, definitely. It's like I said before with the recruiter email. That happens all the time. If I get an email from a client and it just says "Can we talk?" with no context, my heart immediately drops into my stomach. I'm instantly convinced they're terminating my contract. Which, you know, contract work is so precarious anyway. You don't get benefits, you don't get PTO. I had to buy my own health insurance on the exchange this year, and let me tell you, navigating that website is a nightmare. It's like it was designed in 1998. The UI is terrible, the drop-down menus don't work on mobile... I don't understand how they spent millions of dollars on a system that crashes if you click the back button. 

I actually thought about offering to consult for them, just to fix their frontend. I know a guy who did some government contracting for the DMV, and he said it's basically a license to print money because they have no idea how long anything should actually take to code. He bought a Tesla with the money from one project. Though, honestly, I don't get the hype with Teslas. The build quality is awful. Have you seen the panel gaps on those things? And the touchscreen controls for everything—what if the screen freezes and you just want to turn on the windshield wipers? It's a safety hazard. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Minor things. Yeah, a delayed email or a vague Slack message, and I'm instantly spiraling, convinced I'm about to lose everything, even though 99% of the time they just want to ask a question about a database query. It's exhausting.
Do you find it really hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might not make sense?

Yeah, that's exactly why I came in. I just can't shut my brain off anymore. It's like a runaway train. It starts with one little thing, like... like a client not responding to an email. And then within minutes, I'm entirely convinced I'm going to lose the contract, and then I'm going to fall behind on my divorce payments, and then I'll just never get back to a real leadership role again. 

Which, speaking of the divorce payments, my ex-wife's lawyer is a real piece of work. The guy wears these ridiculous bow ties, like he thinks he's Tucker Carlson or something. Who wears a bow tie to a mediation session? And he's always using these condescending little phrases like "Well, if we look at the equitable distribution matrix..." It's just a spreadsheet, Todd, you didn't invent cold fusion. But she hired him because he's supposedly a shark. Honestly, I think she just likes that his office is in one of those fancy glass buildings downtown with the espresso machine in the waiting room. The espresso is terrible, by the way. It's one of those pod machines. You can't get a proper crema from a pod. I bought this Italian semi-automatic machine last year, a Rocket Appartamento, beautiful machine, stainless steel... takes like twenty minutes to heat up, though, which is a pain when you just want a quick shot before a meeting.

But yeah, anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the worrying. Yeah, I know it doesn't make sense to jump from a delayed email to total financial ruin, but I just can't stop it. Once it starts, my brain just completely takes over.
Have you experienced anxiety or worry even during times when there wasn’t anything specific happening in your life that would normally cause stress?

Yeah, absolutely. Even on a Saturday when I'm just sitting on the couch and no one's emailing me, I still feel wound up pretty much all day. It's like my shoulders are just completely locked up, and I'm just sitting there waiting for bad news to drop. I end up pacing around the house, or if I'm on a call, I'm bouncing my leg the whole time, even if it's just a casual catch-up. 

Actually, I was doing that last weekend when I was on the phone with my brother. He lives out in Denver now. Moved there a few years ago because he got really into, like, trail running and craft breweries. Which, honestly, the craft beer scene is getting out of hand. Every time I go visit him, he drags me to some warehouse where they serve you a beer that tastes like pine needles and grapefruit juice. And they charge you twelve bucks for a pint! Plus tip! And they don't even have waiters, you have to stand in line at the bar for twenty minutes behind a guy with a handlebar mustache who's asking the bartender about the specific hop varietals. I don't get it. I just want a normal beer. Like a lager. You know, a beer that actually tastes like beer. 

My brother actually tried to get me to go on a trail run with him last time I was there. I told him, "Look at me, do I look like a guy who runs up mountains?" Plus, the altitude out there messes with my head. You get off the plane and suddenly you're out of breath just walking to baggage claim. The Denver airport is bizarre, too. Have you seen those murals they have? And that giant blue horse statue with the glowing red eyes outside? People say there's a secret bunker under the airport for the Illuminati or something. I don't buy into conspiracy theories, but you have to admit, it's a weird vibe for an airport. 

But, uh, anyway... what was the question? Oh, feeling stressed when nothing's happening. Yeah, even when I'm just sitting at home, I'm pacing, my shoulders are tight, and I just can't relax. It's like my body is always on high alert.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like you’re losing control?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. Like a sudden attack out of nowhere? No. It's more of a constant, grinding feeling, you know? Not like a sudden spike where I can't breathe. 

Though, speaking of not being able to breathe, I did have this horrible chest cold back in January. Or maybe it was February? Whenever it was that we had that weird warm spell where it was like 65 degrees for three days and then it snowed a foot. The weather here is completely unhinged lately. You never know if you need a winter coat or a light jacket. I ended up buying this really expensive Gore-Tex shell jacket because I figured it would be versatile, right? Good for rain, good for wind. But the zipper on it is so finicky. You have to line it up perfectly or it just jams. You'd think for four hundred dollars they could put a decent zipper on the thing. YKK zippers, that's the gold standard. I read this whole article about how YKK basically has a monopoly on the zipper market because they make everything in-house, even the brass. It's fascinating, really, how one company can just dominate something so specific. 

But anyway... no, I don't get sudden panic things. Just the constant worrying.
Do you often feel fatigued or low on energy, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Fatigued? No, not really. I mean, I'm tired sometimes, sure, but I don't feel completely wiped out for no reason. 

Although, speaking of energy, I did try to get into that whole keto diet thing a while back to see if it would give me more energy. You know, where you cut out all the carbs and just eat fat and protein? It is incredibly difficult to do if you actually enjoy food. I tried making this "keto bread" out of almond flour and psyllium husk, and it tasted exactly like a kitchen sponge. Just completely dense and flavorless. And don't even get me started on cauliflower rice. People act like if you just put enough soy sauce on it, you won't notice it's cauliflower. You notice. It smells like feet when you cook it. 

I ended up giving up after about two weeks because I was at this Italian place for a work lunch—Luigi's, over on 4th Street, have you been? They do this incredible veal saltimbocca. Anyway, they put the bread basket down, and they had this focaccia with the big flakes of sea salt and rosemary baked right in. I just couldn't do it anymore. I ate like three pieces before the appetizers even came out. The waiter gave me this look, like, "Buddy, pace yourself," but I didn't care. I think those diets are just a scam anyway to sell people expensive supplements. Like those exogenous ketones? Total snake oil.

But, uh, no, I don't really feel physically exhausted or anything like that. Just the mental stuff.

Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (F43.20) is no longer considered likely due to the duration and persistence of symptoms beyond a typical adjustment period and their pervasive, not situational, nature.

You never know if you need a winter coat or a light jacket. I ended up buying this really expensive Gore-Tex shell jacket because I figured it would be versatile, right? Good for rain, good for wind. But the zipper on it is so finicky. You have to line it up perfectly or it just jams. You'd think for four hundred dollars they could put a decent zipper on the thing. YKK zippers, that's the gold standard. I read this whole article about how YKK basically has a monopoly on the zipper market because they make everything in-house, even the brass. It's fascinating, really, how one company can just dominate something so specific. 

But anyway... no, I don't get sudden panic things. Just the constant worrying.

inference.note: The patient continues to describe chronic, persistent worry across multiple domains, physical symptoms of tension and restlessness, and difficulty controlling the worry, consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). There is no evidence of panic attacks or acute episodic anxiety, which would support F41.0 or F41.8. Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (F43.20) remains a possible secondary consideration, especially given the prior job loss and divorce, but the duration and pervasiveness of symptoms suggest a primary anxiety disorder rather than a time-limited adjustment response.

doctor.question: Do you often feel fatigued or low on energy, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

patient.answer:
Fatigued? No, not really. I mean, I'm tired sometimes, sure, but I don't feel completely wiped out for no reason. 

Although, speaking of energy, I did try to get into that whole keto diet thing a while back to see if it would give me more energy. You know, where you cut out all the carbs and just eat fat and protein? It is incredibly difficult to do if you actually enjoy food. I tried making this "keto bread" out of almond flour and psyllium husk, and it tasted exactly like a kitchen sponge. Just completely dense and flavorless. And don't even get me started on cauliflower rice. People act like if you just put enough soy sauce on it, you won't notice it's cauliflower. You notice. It smells like feet when you cook it. 

I ended up giving up after about two weeks because I was at this Italian place for a work lunch—Luigi's, over on 4th Street, have you been? They do this incredible veal saltimbocca. Anyway, they put the bread basket down, and they had this focaccia with the big flakes of sea salt and rosemary baked right in. I just couldn't do it anymore. I ate like three pieces before the appetizers even came out. The waiter gave me this look, like, "Buddy, pace yourself," but I didn't care. I think those diets are just a scam anyway to sell people expensive supplements. Like those exogenous ketones? Total snake oil.

But, uh, no, I don't really feel physically exhausted or anything like that. Just the mental stuff.

inference.note: The patient denied experiencing sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort (ruling out panic attacks), and also denied significant fatigue or low energy. The anxiety remains persistent, generalized, and uncontrolled, aligning with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (F43.20) is no longer considered likely due to the duration and persistence of symptoms beyond a typical adjustment period and their pervasive, not situational, nature.
